## Rationale

Compares Step 069's total-with-explicit-error-codomain transition T:SxE->S-union-Error against Q15's partial delta, hypothesizing they may be representational variants of the same partiality semantics (explicit Error value vs. undefinedness) but explicitly declines to claim equivalence without a formal encoding proof [S1615]. Additionally, Explicitly demotes Step 232's K_{t+1}=T_t(K_t) from historically canonical status to a synthesis-level abstraction over several earlier, semantically distinct strands (delta, tau, R, Update, Revise), since no proof shows T_t can subsume them without semantic loss [S1615]. Further, Produces the mandated reconciliation matrix across 10 historical transition formulations, each scored on signature, primary layer, relationship to Step 232, and verdict (2 compatible candidates, 3 distinct, 2 unresolved, 1 placeholder, 1 partially unresolved, and Step 232 itself marked not yet canonical) -- deliberately avoiding a single unified verdict [S1615]. Relatedly, Traces the root cause of 'Transformation' polysemy to treating mathematically distinct functions (delta, tau, T, R) as though identical despite differing domains, codomains, arities, semantics, failure models and context treatment -- confirming and explaining the polysemy S1614 flagged as a term-overload problem [S1615]. In the same vein, Traces the genealogy of the State symbol itself: the corpus records 7+ distinct formalizations of Knowledge State with state equality left undefined, so K_t=S_t (using two different historical notations interchangeably) cannot be assumed -- S_t may at most be one layer's state representation [S1615]. Argues 'state transition' actually conflates two distinct transitions -- knowledge-object lifecycle (K->K') and epistemic-status transition (e_i->e_j, constrained by the covering relation) -- concluding the abstract K_{t+1}=T(K_t) formulation may be too coarse to explain status evolution on its own [S1615]. Additionally, States the step's central methodological insight: the apparent proliferation of competing transition formulations partly reflects that each answers a genuinely different question (event application, contract-permitted transition, epistemic result of evidence, knowledge revision, federated outcome, abstract state evolution) rather than pure contradiction -- but explicitly refuses to let this insight excuse away the formulations that remain genuinely unresolved competing models rather than merely different layers [S1615].
